land.text: the Kirghiz SSR, 'established as a constituent Union Republic' on 5 December 1936

predecessors.note: 'On 31 August 1991, Kyrgyzstan declared independence from the USSR'; 'On 26 December the Soviet Union ceased to exist.' Cliopatria's row starts in 1992.

capitals.name: Bishkek (Frunze until February 1991)
capitals.note: Infobox Bishkek 42°52'N 74°36'E; 'In February the name of the capital was changed back to its pre-revolutionary name of Bishkek' (1991 in the page's context).

rulers.name: Askar Akayev
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'elected president in October 1990'; resigned in April 2005 after the Tulip Revolution.

rulers.name: Kurmanbek Bakiyev
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'assumed the presidency after winning the July 2005 presidential election'; 'In April 2010, widespread protests erupted against Bakiyev's administration'.

rulers.name: Roza Otunbayeva
rulers.title: Interim president
rulers.note: Led the provisional government from April 2010; the page gives no end date before the 2011 election.

rulers.name: Sooronbay Jeenbekov
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Succeeded Atambayev in 2017; resigned in October 2020.

rulers.name: Sadyr Japarov
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'In January 2021, Japarov was elected president in a landslide victory'; the page does not give his October 2020 acting role. Reviewer: interim president from October 2020, after 'Jeenbekov resigned' ('subsequently appointed as interim president and prime minister'); 'In January 2021, Japarov was elected president'.

correction.text: the Kirghiz SSR's territory, independent from 31 August 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: independence was declared on 31 August 1991 ('Declaration of State Independence'), four months before the Soviet Union 'ceased to exist' on 26 December; Cliopatria's row starts in 1992. The 1992 outline is used for 1991 and overlaps the USSR's last year.

193,003 km2 against the infobox 200,105 km2 (ratio 0.96). One outline for 1992-2023: the China agreement of 1996 and the 2009 final line ('Kyrgyzstan ceded the Uzengi-Kush', China 'giving up part of the Khan Tengri Peak') move strips too small to show on the grid. The page lists the Uzbek enclave Sokh (325 km2), the Kyrgyz exclave Barak and the Tajik exclaves Vorukh and Kayragach; the page says nothing of how an outline should treat them.
Same outline as 1992-2023. In March 2025 Japarov and Rahmon signed an agreement to demarcate the Tajik frontier (after the end year).

region.text: the Kirghiz SSR within its Soviet-era borders, capital Bishkek

ledger.note: 31 August 1991: Kyrgyzstan declares independence from the USSR. 'On 31 August 1991, Kyrgyzstan declared independence from the USSR'; the Supreme Council 'adopted the Declaration of State Independence'.
5 May 1993: the Republic of Kyrgyzstan becomes the Kyrgyz Republic. 'the official name changed from the Republic of Kyrgyzstan to the Kyrgyz Republic'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: the Uzengi-Kush, 'a mountainous area located south of the Issyk Kul region'

ledger.note: 2009: the China border is finalised. 'The border agreement was finalised in 2009, with the People's Republic of China giving up part of the Khan Tengri Peak while Kyrgyzstan ceded the Uzengi-Kush', 'a mountainous area located south of the Issyk Kul region'. The page gives no area; the place is the researcher's reading of the name.

region.text: part of the Khan Tengri Peak

ledger.note: 2009: part of Khan Tengri comes to Kyrgyzstan in the same agreement ('the People's Republic of China giving up part of the Khan Tengri Peak'); the page does not quantify it.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: April 2021: Kyrgyz-Tajik border fighting. 'This conflict then escalated into a three-day battle in April–May 2021, which killed 55 people'; it began as a conflict over water (Tajikistan page: 'In April 2021, a conflict over water with Kyrgyzstan escalated').

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: May 2021: the three-day battle ends; the page gives no ceasefire date or terms.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: 14 September 2022: renewed fighting on 'most of the border'. 'a 14–20 September confrontation that caused 137,000 Kyrgyz civilians to flee'; 'over 100 people, including at least 37 civilians' killed.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: 20 September 2022: the weeklong clashes end ('14–20 September'); no border moved.

wars.name: Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border clashes (2021 and 2022)

zones.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

wars.outcome: No ceasefire terms on the page; neither side gained land. Delimitation agreements followed in 2025 (21 February signing, 13 March agreement; the Tort-Kocho road and a 15 m 'security zone' declared a neutral zone), after the end year.
wars.note: Shared with the republic-of-tajikistan dossier; the page was opened for that dossier and used here for the dates.

certainty.note: The frontier follows the Soviet republic lines; China's was delimited in 1996 and finalised in 2009 (China-Kyrgyzstan page). The page gives no treaty for the Uzbek frontier and parts of the Tajik one were fought over in 2021-2022, so those two frontiers and the enclaves are the exceptions.

notes: Two shapes: one outline for 1992-2023 and the same for 2024 (193,003 km2; gazetteer overlay: 622 of the 660 grid cells of Natural Earth's Kyrgyzstan inside; the 38 outside were not examined). Start 1991 (31 August) rather than Cliopatria's 1992; a new keyframe carries 1991. The 2009 China exchange has no area on the page and is far below the grid; 'Uzengi-Kuush' and 'Khan Tengri' are not in the gazetteer (listed in the report). The 2021 and 2022 clashes are contests with republic-of-tajikistan, matched in that dossier; the exact end of the April-May 2021 battle is not on the page. Not opened (budget): the Uzbek frontier and the enclaves' history, the 2005 Tulip Revolution and the 2010 revolution (not territorial).
